beats.title: Lesson 18 — Hardening the FUXA Login
beats.sub: Closing the HMI door we walked through
beats.say: Welcome back to CybICS. Back in lesson four we brute-forced the FUXA operator interface in a single guess, because it shipped with a default password. In this lesson we play defence and close that door.

beats.head: The weakness: a default HMI password
beats.body:
FUXA ships with the built-in account admin / 123456, and its login API has no lockout.
  • Default credentials on an operator interface are a direct path to process control.
  • The fix is to set a strong, unique password on the admin account.
  • The dashboard verifies it by checking the default login no longer works.
Maps to D3FEND Strong Password Policy.
beats.say: The weakness is a default password on the human machine interface: admin, one two three four five six, with no lockout to slow a guesser down. On an operator interface that is a direct path to controlling the process. The fix is simple: set a strong, unique password on the admin account. And the CybICS dashboard verifies our work by checking that the default login no longer works.

beats.caption: Confirm the weakness: the default HMI login still works
beats.say: First we confirm the problem. We test the default credentials against the FUXA sign-in interface, and they are accepted. The operator interface is wide open to anyone who knows the factory password, which is to say, anyone.

beats.caption: Harden it: set a strong admin password, then re-test the default
beats.say: Now we harden it. As the administrator we set a strong, unique password on the account, and immediately re-test the default. This time the default is rejected. In a real deployment you would do this in the FUXA settings, under user management; here our tool drives the same change through the interface's own A P I.

beats.caption: Verify the defense in the CybICS dashboard - on the attack machine
beats.say: On the dashboard we open the harden FUXA login challenge and click verify defence. The check tries the default credentials, confirms they are now rejected, and marks the defence complete.

beats.head: What we learned
beats.body:
• Change every default credential before an HMI goes on the network.
  • Use strong, unique passwords, and add lockout and multi-factor where the software allows.
  • Keep the HMI on an isolated network so a stolen or guessed login cannot be reached in the first place.
beats.say: To recap: change every default credential before an operator interface goes on the network, use strong unique passwords, and add lockout and multi factor authentication where the software allows it. And keep the human machine interface on an isolated network, so that even a guessed login cannot be reached from where an attacker sits.

beats.title: Defense verified: CybICS(FUXA_s3cur3d)
beats.sub: Next lessons: firewalling and segmenting the control network  ·  github.com/mniedermaier/CybICS
beats.say: Defence verified. The operator interface no longer opens to a default password. In the final defensive lessons we put the controller behind a firewall and segment the network around it.
